subtype: Friend or partner on the receiving end [Receiver]
passage: In the university hostel, Wasim had loved rooming with Thomas at first. Thomas called him "the smartest guy on the floor" and dragged him to every party. By second term it was different. When Wasim got a B, Thomas laughed: "Guess I'm the brains now." When Thomas lost the room key, it was Wasim's fault. When Wasim talked about his grandfather being unwell, Thomas turned the talk to his own football trial. Wasim started double-checking everything he said. One evening the hostel warden, Mr Pinto, found him sitting on the stairs. "You've gone very quiet this term." Wasim hesitated, then told him. Mr Pinto listened. "None of that sounds like your fault. Let's talk about a room change, and keep talking."

qa.q: What did Thomas call Wasim at first?
qa.a: He called him "the smartest guy on the floor".

qa.q: How did Wasim feel by second term, and what shows it?
qa.a: He felt small and unsure of himself; he started double-checking everything he said.

qa.q: What turning point came on the stairs?
qa.a: Wasim told the warden what was happening, and Mr Pinto said it wasn't his fault and offered to talk about a room change, giving him an outside view.

qa.q: How might Mr Pinto see Wasim's quietness this term?
qa.a: He saw it as a sign something was wrong, which is why he checked in gently.

grounding: A student flattered early by a self-centred roommate grows small and blamed, and recognises the pattern with a trusted warden.

subtype: Friend or partner on the receiving end [Receiver]
passage:
Dear Rashmi-di,
You're the only one I can say this to. When I met Kunal in first year, he told everyone I was the cleverest girl in college. I felt like I was glowing. Now, a year later, I don't recognise myself. If I talk about my day, he talks over me. When he forgot my birthday, somehow I ended up apologising for "making it a big deal". Last week I cried after he called my painting "cute for a beginner", and he said I was too sensitive. I've started believing him. Maybe I am. Is it me?
Can I come home this weekend and talk properly? I think I need someone outside all this to tell me what they see.
Love,
Trisha

qa.q: What did Kunal call Trisha's painting?
qa.a: He called it "cute for a beginner".

qa.q: What is Trisha doubting now, and why?
qa.a: She doubts herself, wondering if she is too sensitive, because Kunal keeps blaming her and she has started believing him.

qa.q: What choice does Trisha make in this letter, and why is it wise?
qa.a: She reaches out to Rashmi-di, a trusted outsider, to talk properly, which can help her see the pattern clearly.

qa.q: How might Rashmi feel reading "Is it me?"
qa.a: She may feel worried and protective, and keen to reassure Trisha and help her see what is happening.

grounding: A young woman flattered early by a partner now feels small, blamed and unheard, and turns to a trusted cousin to see the pattern.
